title: Staged reopen & tenant-priority throttling playbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a multi-hour hosted API capacity event on 2025-02-18 we observed persistent GPU pool depletion that caused large request queues, tenant-level throttling, and cascading timeouts. This ticket defines a staged reopen (unthrottle) playbook that prioritizes tenant fairness, minimizes re-triggering surge behavior, and provides operational runbooks and telemetry to safely restore capacity and validate recovery. The goal is to ship automation and runbook changes that let SREs reopen pools in a controlled fashion and prevent immediate re-exhaustion.
impact_summary: Impacted customers experienced higher latency and 5xx rates for generation and chat endpoints for ~2.5 hours. Several medium-tier customers saw elevated error budgets and a small number of enterprise customers reported production interruptions to critical features. Total request backlog peaked at 220k requests queued across pools.
detection_timeline: 2025-02-18: 02:14 UTC - Alert: gpu-pool-saturation. 02:18 UTC - Increase in queued requests per-pool dashboard. 02:25 UTC - First escalations to SRE and runtime-oncall. 02:42 UTC - Temporary throttles applied to burst traffic; downstream timeouts rise. 04:30 UTC - Partial pool priming and tenant isolation steps started. 05:00 UTC - Capacity stabilized after progressive drain and forced preemption.
root_cause: Primary cause: a sudden increase in long-sequence generation traffic from a small set of customers combined with a regression in our autoscaler hysteresis that delayed new GPU allocation. Secondary contributor: prefix cache TTL configuration caused recurrent cold-start overhead for certain models increasing per-request GPU time. The autoscaler backoff prevented timely prewarm of reserved instances.
immediate_actions: Applied emergency tenant caps for top 8 bursty tenants to reduce queue amplification
Manually enabled opportunistic prewarm on a subset of compatible GPU nodes to drain KV cache misses
Rolled back autoscaler hysteresis change from 2025-02-10 that lengthened scale-up windows
Triage note: customers affected were contacted by CS; incident timeline posted to internal slack and incident channel
proposed_action_items: Implement a staged-unthrottle orchestration that reopens pool capacity in waves with tenant-priority levels (stage 0: system, stage 1: enterprise, stage 2: paid, stage 3: free). Each stage has a configurable max QPS and ramp duration
Add a tenant-reserve token bucket to ensure in-flight high-priority requests retained low latency during reopen
Introduce detection-based prewarm: when queue growth crosses threshold X for Y minutes, trigger prewarm jobs for model variants fingerprinted in the backlog
Fix autoscaler hysteresis: change to adaptive backoff that shortens scale-up delay when sustained queue growth is detected
Lower KV cache cold-start penalty: reduce TTL reset behavior for known long-sequence prompts and preload popular prefixes during prewarm
Create a one-click SRE console action to run staged-unthrottle with safeguards and simulated dry-run mode
Post-incident evaluation: run chaos tests (synthetic tenant surge) against the playbook in staging to validate re-exhaustion protection
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook automation can reopen a drained pool to 60% capacity within N minutes without queue growing above pre-event baseline for sustained 10 minutes. 2) Staged reopen respects tenant priorities and rate-limits lower tiers automatically. 3) Telemetry dashboards show meaningful signals: per-stage QPS, queue delta, prewarm success rate, and model cold-start latency. 4) SRE dry-run executes without modifying live traffic and produces expected prewarm plan.
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): implement and test playbook against synthetic surges. Phase B (canary): deploy to single non-critical region and allow live traffic with 'dry-run' toggled off for 1 hour during low traffic window. Phase C (global): enable playbook as on-call tool with roll-forward automation. Each phase includes 48h observation window and rollback criteria documented in runbook.
telemetry_changes: Add new panels to Console: staged_unthrottle_status, per_stage_throughput, queue_delta_by_tenant, prewarm_job_success_rate, autoscaler_scale_up_latency. Emit events for staged_unthrottle.start and staged_unthrottle.complete. Create alert that fires if post-unthrottle queue growth rate > 2x for 10m.
